courts.name: Common Court of Justice and Arbitration (Cour Commune de Justice et d'Arbitrage, CCJA)
courts.note: Art. 14 as revised in 2008: ensures common interpretation and application of the Treaty, its regulations, the Uniform Acts and decisions; hears cassation from States Parties' courts in Uniform Act and regulation cases, and on quashing decides the merits itself. Art. 20: its judgments are res judicata and enforceable in every State Party like national decisions; in the same case no contrary decision may be enforced there. Art. 20 was not amended in 2008.

member_routes.note: National courts try these cases at first instance and on appeal (art. 13). Cassation against their appellate or final decisions lies to the CCJA in place of the national cassation court, not for decisions applying criminal sanctions (art. 14). A party may apply directly, or a national cassation court may refer the case (art. 15). Referral suspends national cassation proceedings until the CCJA declines competence (art. 16). A party that contested a national cassation court's competence may apply within two months; a decision given without competence is void (art. 18).
Art. 14 para. 2: national courts hearing cases under art. 13 may ask the CCJA for an advisory opinion (avis consultatif). The Treaty says nothing about the opinion's effect on the court that asked.
